D018-D001_h024.question: It feels like my brain is always buzzing, but not in a good way. I'm 29, and for the past year or so, it’s been really hard to focus on anything, especially at work. I'll be writing some ad copy, and suddenly, I'm just… not there. It’s like a movie reel playing in my head, seeing things I wish I could forget. When I’m not lost in those moments, I just feel this crushing guilt, this sense of "what ifs" that never leaves. Even when something good happens, like smashing a campaign goal, I just… don't feel happy. It's like joy is a foreign concept now. And my temper… it’s a hair trigger. The smallest thing can set me off, and I’ll just explode, then feel awful about it afterward. I don’t know what’s happening to me.

D018-D001_h025.question:
It’s like my mind is a broken record, constantly skipping back to that time, you know? Even certain smells, or a specific tone of voice, can make my heart pound and my hands sweat, like it’s all happening again. I try to push it down, to not feel anything, but then everything feels so… empty. I can design the most beautiful piece of jewelry, yet feel absolutely nothing about it afterwards. My work used to bring me so much joy.

My divorce was tough, and I still feel this gnawing shame, even though it’s been a few years now. Like it was all my fault, that I should have done something differently. That’s probably why I’ve been so snappy with my assistant lately. I just blurt things out, harsh words, and can’t seem to hold back, even when I know it’s unfair. My concentration has been shot too, lately, I can barely focus on a design for more than a few minutes. It makes me wonder if I'm losing my touch.

    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D001_h025.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
